question:
A 22-year-old man comes to the physician because of several episodes of painless bloody urine over the past 6 months. The episodes are not related to physical activity. He has had frequent nosebleeds since early childhood and an episode of heavy bleeding after a tooth extraction one year ago. He smokes one pack of cigarettes daily. He drinks 1 to 2 beers on social occasions. He appears pale. His vital signs are within normal limits. Physical examination shows several small hematomas in different stages of healing over his arms and legs. Examination of the extremities shows decreased passive range of motion with crepitus in both ankles. His abdomen is soft and nontender. Laboratory studies show:
Hemoglobin 9.5 mg/dL
Leukocyte count 5000/mm3
Platelet count 240,000/mm3
Bleeding time 5 minutes
Prothrombin time 14 seconds
Partial thromboplastin time 68 seconds
Urine
RBC 30–40/hpf
RBC casts negative
WBC none
Protein negative
An x-ray of the pelvis shows no abnormalities. Further evaluation of this patient is most likely to show which of the following findings?"?

options.opa: Evasive behavior when asked about the hematomas
options.opb: Palpable spleen below the left costal margin

reasoning_chain: CHAIN: Chronic episodes of painless bloody urine -> frequent nosebleeds since childhood -> heavy bleeding after tooth extraction -> smoking one pack of cigarettes daily -> drinking 1 to 2 beers on social occasions -> pale appearance -> small hematomas in different stages of healing over arms and legs -> decreased passive range of motion with crepitus in both ankles -> laboratory findings of low hemoglobin, normal leukocyte count, normal platelet count, prolonged bleeding time, prolonged prothrombin time, prolonged partial thromboplastin time -> 80%
enhanced_information: The patient's presentation with chronic painless bloody urine, frequent nosebleeds, heavy bleeding history, smoking, alcohol use, pale appearance, small hematomas, and joint symptoms is indicative of a bleeding disorder. Laboratory findings support this with low hemoglobin, normal leukocyte and platelet counts, and prolonged bleeding and clotting times. Further evaluation is likely to show intraarticular iron deposition due to the joint symptoms and bleeding history, rather than other options like evasive behavior, palpable spleen, nephrolithiasis, or hemosiderin-laden alveolar macrophages.
analysis: The patient's presentation with chronic painless bloody urine, frequent nosebleeds, heavy bleeding history, smoking, alcohol use, pale appearance, small hematomas, and joint symptoms is indicative of a bleeding disorder. Laboratory findings support this with low hemoglobin, normal leukocyte and platelet counts, and prolonged bleeding and clotting times. Given the joint symptoms and bleeding history, the most likely finding on further evaluation would be intraarticular iron deposition.
